CH3COCOOH + CoA + NAD+ → CO2 + CH3-CO-CoA + NADH + H+

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. questions.stem: Challenge question. The land plants process about 123 billion tons of carbon (about 15% of the total atmospheric CO2) each year. How many tons of CO2 do the plants remove from the air, and how much CO2 is in the atmosphere? (Ref: Beer C et al. Science 2010; 329(5993):834-8). Note: The C atom accounts for 27.3% of the mass of CO2 molecules.

options.text: 45,000/ 300,000 Photosynthesis: Light-dependent reactions

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. 123 billion tons of carbon is present in 123/0.273= 450.5 billion tons of CO2. 450.5 billion tons is 15% of the total atmospheric CO2. Thus, the atmosphere has about 451 billion tons/0.15= 3,007 billion tons of CO2.

questions.stem: Bacteria generate 200 million tons, and humans generate 85 million tons of nitrogen compounds by fixing atmospheric nitrogen every year. Why do humans fix nitrogen?

options.text: Nitrogen compounds created by bacteria are inferior or not available to human use.
Nitrogen compounds produced by bacteria are not enough to meet current demand.
Nitrogen compounds created by bacteria are more expensive than those created by humans.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Nitrogen fixed by bacteria is taken by trees and crop plants, thus, it becomes readily available to humans. Bacteria and humans produce the same compound (NH3) by fixing nitrogen. Bacteria fix nitrogen for free, while human-fixed nitrogen is expensive (it requires air and natural gas to react at 3000 PSI at 500 degrees C).

questions.stem: Why is bacterial sulfur acquisition not considered sulfur fixation?

options.text: Because organic sulfur is abundant in soil.
Because sulfur compounds exist as solid chemicals, not as gases.
Because bacteria directly import sulfur compounds in soil capillaries.
Because absorbable sulfur compounds are already available in soil and water.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. Sulfur is not an inert element; sulfur compounds are plentiful in soil; microbes usually break (do not need to fix or synthesize) sulfur compounds before absorbing the sulfur compounds.

Sulfur is abundant in the Earth's cr...] SECOND CHECK (his slides, OpenStax, Exam 2 study guide): The slide lists H2S (a gas) as a sulfur source, which further undercuts B ('solid chemicals, not gases'); the text's 'abundant ... not a limiting factor' plus 'absorb soluble sulfate' supports D. questions.stem: Grossly, which of the phases of the eukaryotic cell cycle is somewhat equivalent to the B period of the bacterial cell cycle?

options.text: S phase.
M phase.
G1 phase.
Interphase.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. In the G1 phase and B period, the cell carries out all metabolic activities but does not replicate DNA. B- M phase is somewhat similar to the D period (the cell divides). D- interphase may be somewhat similar to the C period combined with the B period (the cell does not divide in those phases).

questions.stem: If a eukaryotic cell receives a mitogenic signal, the cell enters ______ and replicates DNA.

options.text: S phase
M phase
G1 phase
C period
D period Replication of chromosomal DNA

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A. Eukaryotic cells normally live in the G1 phase (they do not replicate DNA at this phase). The cell replicates DNA mostly in the S phase and divides and distributes chromosomes to the daughter cells during the M phase. Bacterial cells normally live in B period (the cells do not replicate DNA at this period), replicate DNA during the C period, and divide and distribute chromosomes to the daughter cells during the D period. The bacterial cell cycle is not fully understood.

Medium contains sodium thioglycolate.
Plates incubated in an oxygen-free/nitrogen-rich atmosphere.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A. It is appropriate for growing capnophiles (that need low oxygen and high CO2 conditions. B- to remove dissolved oxygen. C- to remove atmospheric oxygen.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the stationary phase of a bacterial growth curve?

options.text: In this phase, the death rate is high, and the growth rate is low.
In this phase, the death and growth rates are nearly identical.
In this phase, the death rate is negligible, the growth rate is fixed and high.
In this phase, the death rate is negligible, and the growth rate is negligible or very low.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. A- declining phase; C- log phase; D- lag phase.

questions.stem: One should harvest bacterial cells at the _______ phase to isolate biologically active enzymes, and ________ phase to extract antibiotics.

options.text: lag/log
log/stationary
stationary/declining
declining/prolonged declining

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Cell express primary metabolites (such as enzymes) during the log phase and secondary metabolites, including antibiotics, during the stationary and declining phases.

questions.stem: A scientist wants to maintain the log phase growth condition of a strain of Escherichia coli indefinitelshould y. What the scientists do? Note: She must keep the culture uncontaminated.

options.text: Nothing, it is impossible in a closed system.
The scientist should grow the bacterium in a small pond.
The scientists should oxygenate the culture by bubbling filtered air.
The scientist should remove some culture and replenish the volume with a fresh medium.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D, adding fresh nutrients and removing toxic substances allow the perpetual log phase.

The scientist plated 100 microliters of the diluted sample (v) on a plate. What was the dilution factor (df)?
questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. The dilution factors are (i) Stock sample -0, (ii) 1 ml of stock sample+ 9 ml of LB broth- 10, mixed; (iii) 1 ml of diluted sample ii + 9 ml of LB broth-100, mixed; (iv) 1 ml of diluted sample iii+ 9 ml of LB broth, mixed- 1000; (v) 1 ml of diluted sample iv+ 9 ml of LB broth, mixed- 10,000.

Note: make a significant colony count. Please use the formula N= (n/v) x df, where N is the bacterial count/ml of the original sample, n is the number of colonies grown in the plate, v is the volume of liquid plated and df is the dilution factor.
questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. The formula is N= (n/v)xd.

questions.stem: A600 of an E. coli culture in LB broth was 0.5. The culture is currently at the _______ phase of the growth curve.

options.text: lag
log
stationary
declining

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. A- should be less than 0.1, C or D if A600 were >1.0.

questions.stem: A 100 ml sample of pond water was filtered using a 0.4-micron filter paper, and the filter paper was exposed to a MacConkey agar plate. 120 bacterial colonies developed after overnight incubation of the plate. What is the bacterial count of the pond water, and what type of bacteria were counted by the protocol?

options.text: 1.20 cfu/ml, G(-) bacteria that can grow in MacConkey agar plate.
120 cfu/ ml, all types of bacteria present in the pond water.
1,200 cfu/ml, G(-) bacteria present in the pond water.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A, because 120 CFU in 100 ml water= 1.2 cfu/ml; also because the plate has a selective-differential medium (some bacteria in the pond water failed to grow in the plate).

questions.stem: A person treated a surgical knife with 10% Clorox® solution. She performed _______.

options.text: sanitizing
sterilization
disinfection
pasteurization
antisepsis

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C, by definition (removing microbes from inanimate objects). Sanitizing- decontaminating cooking pots and utensils; sterilization- inactivating all microbes; pasteurization- reducing microbe counts from liquid substances, E- removing microbes from skin surface.

questions.stem: Pasteurization is technically comparable to which of these?

options.text: HLD.
ILD.
LLD.
UHLD.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, because it removes all or most of the vegetative microbes and viruses, but not endospores. D- there is no such category.

questions.stem: Which of the following definitions is CORRECT?

options.text: Commercial Sterilization: Sufficient treatment to inactivate Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Degerming: Mechanical removal of microbes from the surface of live tissues.
Disinfection: Removal of vegetative pathogens from skin surfaces.
Antisepsis: Removal of pathogens from surfaces of utensils.
Sterilization: Removal of all vegetative cells.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, by definition. Other definitions: A- inactivate the Clostridium botulinum endospores, C- removal of microbes from inanimate surfaces, D- removal of microbes from live tissue surfaces, E- removal of all microbes including bacterial endospores.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is technically correct?

options.text: The higher the number of microbes, the faster the killing.
The higher the amount of biofilm, the faster the rate of killing.
When Mycobacterium and naked viruses are inactivated, the surface is completely disinfected.
High-intensity treatment with a short exposure time is equivalent to low-intensity treatment with a long exposure time.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D, as per experimental data. The matching second part for the first of the other statements: A- the slower the killing, B- slower the rate of killing, C- the surface is partially disinfected.

questions.stem: The membrane, proteins, and DNA are the major targets for inactivating microbes. If you destroy the plasma membrane of a cellular microbe, which of the following aspects will be immediately affected?

options.text: All metabolic activities will collapse.
Biological homeostasis will collapse.
Protein synthesis and processing will collapse.
Energy (ATP) synthesis/acquisition will collapse.
Genome replication and transcription will collapse.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Membrane damage would lead to loss of ions and water balance, and that would lead to loss of the membrane potential, and that would kill the cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a valid definition of D value?

options.text: Time of heat treatment needed to reduce the number of microbes of a sample by one log.
Intensity of treatment needed to reduce the number of microbes of a sample by 90%.
Reduction of the number of microbes of a sample to ~10 to the power 0 (i.e., 1)
Two of these definitions are valid.
All these definitions are valid.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D, by definition, D value means the decimal reduction time. One log reduction is the same as a 90% reduction. Option C is incorrect because it is the goal, not the definition, of the D value.

questions.stem: After one D-value of treatment, the bacterial count in a batch of soup was 100,000/liter. What would be the bacterial count after three more D-value equivalents of treatment?

options.text: 1,000/liter.
100/liter.
10/liter.
0/liter.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. After each D-value equivalent of treatment, 10% of the bacterial count will remain, or 0.1. The bacterial count after the first treatment will be 100,00x0.1= 10,000, after second, it will be 10,000x0.1= 1,000; and after 3rd, it will be 1000x0.1= 100.

questions.stem: A stainless-steel dental probe to be used in cleaning teeth should be treated with ___________ and an endoscope (made of plastic tubing) should receive a _________.

options.text: HLD/ILD
ILD/LLD
HLD/LLD
Autoclaving/HLD

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. For dental probe, HLD is not recommended because the probe is made of stable metal and it will touch blood; for an endoscope that cannot be autoclaved, it also touches blood, so it should receive HLD.

questions.stem: In theory, a tongue depressor is considered a __________ item, and a dental probe used for teeth cleaning is considered a __________ item.

options.text: critical/ semi-critical
semi-critical/ critical
non-critical/non-critical
non-critical/ semi-critical

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, because a tongue depressor touches mucous membrane (thus it is a semi-critical item). A dental probe may come in contact with injured gum and blood (thus it is a critical item). However, since the oral mucus membrane of some patients can be injured, medical practitioners would consider a tongue depressor to be a critical item.

options.text: bacterial or fungal spores
enveloped viruses
protozoan cysts
fungal hyphae
naked viruses Hand washing

preparing food and examining patients
waking up from sleep and using restrooms
touching garbage, animals, animal food, and animal waste

questions.stem: Which of the following is recommended for general handwashing?

options.text: Use bar soap.
Rinse hands after lathering.
Take soap before wetting hands.
Use a filter-free forced-air hand drier.
Lather hands thoroughly for 10 seconds.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Other options: A- use an uncontaminated liquid soap (or a newly unpacked bar soap and discard it after use), B- wet hands before taking soap; C- use a clean towel or forced-air drier equipped with an antimicrobial filter; E- lather hands for 20 seconds.

questions.stem: One should not use a hand sanitizers to clean hands if _______________.

options.text: its ingredients include triclosan or triclocarban
the alcohol content of the sanitizer is >75%
its ingredients include polyacrylate
one’s hands are visibly dirty

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D, as per CDC directives. One would use hand sanitizers only if soap and water are unavailable or when using soap and water is not feasible. Some people are sensitive to isopropyl alcohol, polyacrylate, triclosan, or triclocarban; those people should avoid the sanitizers that contain such ingredients. Almost all hand sanitizers contain polyacrylate. The alcohol content of effective hand sanitizers can be as high as 95%.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of medical handwashing?

options.text: Remove all microbes from hands.
Reduce the microbe counts on hands.
Remove the environmental microbes but not the resident microbes on hand.
Remove the environmental microbes and the resident microbes that may readily shed from the hands.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. Removing all microbes from the hands is impossible. Option B is correct but not detailed enough. Option C is the goal of general handwashing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is part of medical handwashing but not general handwashing?

options.text: Using liquid hand soap.
Scrubbing for a minimum of 20 seconds.
Using iodinated soap and sponge scrubbers.
Wiping washed hands with a clean paper towel.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. Plain liquid soap and 20-second scrubbing are not sufficient for medical hand washing, and medically washed hands should be wiped using sterile fabric.

Radioactivity.
No food or drinks.

questions.stem: Which of these is needed to prepare steam heated to 121-135 °C in an autoclave or a cooking pot?

options.text: Water used must be soft, pure, and free of any suspended contaminants.
The altitude must be higher than 1,000 meters above sea level.
The pressure inside the container must be 15 PSI or higher.
The container's volume must expand when heated.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. Barometric pressure of an open pot at sea level is 14.7; water boils at 100 degrees C at this pressure. To heat water above 100oC, pressure must be increased. It takes about 28 atmospheres of presreach achieve 135 °C. Other options: A- is incorrect because pure water boils at a lower temperature compared to water containing dissolved chemicals; B- is incorrect because barometric pressure is lower at higher altitudes, so water would boil at a lower temperature at a higher altitude; D- incorrect because if the volume of a sealed container increases, the pressure would not increase and thus boiling temperature of water would not increase.

questions.stem: A lab technician is using an autoclave to sterilize a bottle of bacterial growth medium and some surgical knives. Which of the following should/could the technician do?

options.text: Wrap the knives with aluminum foil and mark the pack with heat-sensitive tape.
Open the autoclave door as soon as the treatment cycles are over.
Tightly cap the bottle containing bacterial growth medium.
Set the autoclave to operate on the liquid cycle.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D, to prevent boil-over of the liquid items. Other options: A- violation: Aluminum foil is not porous (the packed item may not come in contact to steam and may not get sterilized), B- violation, may cause boil-over and scalding injury, so the technician should wait until the steam in the autoclave is exhausted; C- violation, the bottle would explode.

questions.stem: Which of the following tests ensures that an item has been autoclaved properly?

options.text: The stripes of the autoclave tape on the item have been darkened.
The autoclave sensor printout shows that the cycles went as expected.
The color of the spore test ampules (autoclaved with the item) has not changed after two days.
The color of the spore test ampules (autoclaved with the item) has turned yellow after two days.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. Other options: A- it indicates that the item was exposed to high temperature, but it does not ensure that the items have been sterilized; B- the printout is most likely a good indicator, but the sensors may fail if not properly calibrated; D- the color change to yellow indicates that the endospores germinated (the endospores survived autoclaving) and the autoclave malfunctioned.

questions.stem: Food industries use the high-temperature short-time (HTST) method of pasteurizing milk. Which of the following is an HTST treatment?

options.text: Heating 63oC for 30 minutes.
Heating 72oC for 15 seconds.
Autoclaving at 121oC for 1 minute.
Heating 140-150oC for one second and then rapidly cooling down.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, by definition. Other options: A- is the traditional method of pasteurization, C- not a method of pasteurization; D- is the ultrahigh temperature (UHT) method of pasteurization.

questions.stem: Milk is pasteurized and not autoclaved (to increase shelf life) and to____________, fish or meat is frozen before consuming raw to ________.

options.text: reduce cost of preservation/
enhance nutritional quality/ inactivate viruses and bacteria
preserve flavor and consistency/ to kill worm larvae and eggs Physical methods: Electromagnetic radiation

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. Cost is a concern, but autoclaving would destroy flavor and coagulate proteins, thus reduce flavor and nutritional values to some extent.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about electromagnetic waves is a mismatch?

options.text: Laser (visible) light: Utilizes heat to kill some bacteria in live tissues.
UV light (254 nm): Ionizes water and creates highly reactive oxygen radicals.
Microwave oven: Utilizes heat and not damaging electromagnetic radiation to kill microbes.
Gamma and X-radiation: Ionize water, the resulting free radicals cause single- and double-stranded DNA breaks.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. UV light works by cross-linking (creating new covalent bonds between various functional groups of) macromolecules. Note that very short wavelength UV radiation (100-120 nm) may ionize water molecules and act like ionizing radiation.
questions.priorRationale: CORRECTED AFTER OLQ 7: you picked the microwave statement (my changed answer, and the pick of both outside AI reviewers) and Canvas marked it wrong. So the mismatch is one of the other three. The original key, B ("UV light (254 nm): ionizes water"), is the one that is wrong in real physics: 254 nm UV is non-ionizing and damages DNA by cross-linking bases, even though his Ch 7 text says UVC "may ionize water". Gamma/X-ray (D) is a true statement, and laser heat (A) is the runner-up. WHY NOT 100%: nothing states which option he keyed; B is the best remaining.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the main reason for electron beam irradiation being preferred to gamma irradiation? Note: a Cobalt-60 or Cesium-137 sources were used for gamma radiation.

options.text: Gamma irradiation requires the construction of continuous operation plants.
Gamma irradiation creates harmful chemicals inside the treated food items.
Gamma irradiation plants produce difficult to dispose of radioactive waste.
Gamma irradiation cannot be used in treating food items.
Gamma irradiation is less penetrative than E-beam.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C, it creates waste containing spent radioactive nuclides. Other options: A- both gamma radiation and E-beam requires the construction of a continuous operation plant; B- Cobalt-60 or Cesium-137 sources used for the purpose do not produce harmful chemical inside food items; D- electron beam cannot be used in treating food items, while gamma radiation can be used for the purpose; E- gamma radiation is more penetrative than E-beam, but gamma radiation treatment is slower than electron beam treatment.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be sterilized using short-wavelength UV radiation (of 254 nm wavelength)?

options.text: The air of a laminar flow hood, and a thin film of flowing water.
Bacteria in a covered Petri dish or a capped tube.
Interior of an empty capped bottle.
Carcass of a mouse.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A. UV radiation (of 254 nm wavelength) may not penetrate through thin plastic or paper.

sections.heading: Physical methods: Sound energy, pressure, and filtration

questions.stem: Why is high-pressure pasteurization (87,000 atmospheres) preferred to heat pasteurization (60 °C for 30 minutes) of fruit juices?

options.text: High-pressure pasteurization decontaminates by denaturing proteins.
High-pressure pasteurization is less expensive and technically less challenging.
High-pressure pasteurization increases shelf life and delays spoilage more effectively.
High-pressure pasteurization preserves the delicate flavor and labile nutrients more effectively.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. Both processes deactivate proteins and enzymes, and both increase shelf life; high-pressure pasteurization is more technically challenging.

questions.stem: Cavitation may do each of the following EXCEPT _____________.

options.text: remove attached organic molecules from a metal surface
cause dissolved macromolecules to form floccules
create shock waves and release some heat energy
create microscopic bubbles inside the cells

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, it rather causes the macromolecules to break into smaller fractions.

questions.stem: A size exclusion filter with a nominal pore size of 0.45 micrometers would retain ___________ and larger entities.

options.text: macromolecules such as dissolved proteins
eukaryotic microbes
viruses and satellites
all cellular microbes

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, because eukaryotic microbes are >1.0 micrometer in diameter. Almost all viruses and some bacteria (such as bacteria lacking cell walls such as the genus Mycoplasma) would pass through the filter. Removal of macromolecules requires ultrafilters.

sections.heading: Chemical methods: Alcohols, biguanides, and phenolics

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is CORRECT about alcohols as a disinfectant/antiseptic?

options.text: Alcohols work by forming excess hydrogen bonds
100% ethanol is a better antiseptic than 70% ethanol.
Chronic exposure to ethanol and isopropanol can cause cancer.
Methanol and ethylene glycol are suitable alternatives to ethanol and isopropanol.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. Liquid ethanol can cause oral cancers, and the vapor of isopropanol may cause nasal cancers. Other options: A- incorrect, alcohols are chaotropic agents, which prevent hydrogen bond formation; B- incorrect because pure alcohol does not interact with proteins as rapidly as 75-85% alcohol; D- incorrect because methanol (used in car windshield washer) and ethylene glycol (used in car radiator fluid) are antimicrobial but poisonous to humans.

questions.stem: Phenolics and phenol both work by ___________, but phenolics are much ______ than phenol.

options.text: denaturing proteins and the membrane/ less caustic
destroying polysaccharides/ easier to manufacture
destroying nucleic acids/ more expensive
cross-linking proteins/ more effective

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A, as observed. The other options are factually incorrect.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about biguanides, such as chlorhexidine?

options.text: Pseudomonas aeruginosa may grow in mouthwash solutions preserved by chlorhexidine.
The agents are generally less toxic and non-carcinogenic, but they may cause deafness.
The agents are more effective on G(-) bacteria than G(+) bacteria and fungi.
The agents act by binding the bacterial cell wall and disrupting the membrane.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. The agents are effective on G(+) bacteria at lower concentrations (2 micrograms/ml); for G(-) bacteria and fungi, the needed concentration is about 10-40 fold higher.

questions.stem: In terms of biochemical effects, aldehydes and epoxides are somewhat comparable to which of these physical methods of disinfection?

options.text: moist heat
UV radiation.
Gamma radiation.
Ultrahigh pressure.
Ultrasonic sound waves.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, because these agents act by cross-linking (creating unusual covalent bonds between) various functional groups of the molecules.

questions.stem: Of the halogens, _______ is most suitable for swimming pools, and ______is the most frequently used antiseptic for surgical cleaning purposes.

options.text: fluorine/ chlorine
chorine/ bromine
bromine/ iodine
iodine/ chlorine

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C, because bromine is most stable and least irritating; fluorine is toxic and excessively reactive; chlorine is irritant and gets rapidly used up; and iodine is non-irritating and non-toxic on skin and wounds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is bleaching powder, the agent most frequently used in treating municipal supply water?

options.text: A mixture of CaOCl2, CaCl2, and CaO2Cl2.
NaOCl2.
NH2Cl.
ClO2.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A. Other options: B- sodium hypochlorite (the active ingredient of Clorox®), C- chloramine gas, D- chlorine oxide gas. All these can be used in water treatment.

questions.stem: Many municipalities add small amounts of sodium monophosphofluoride to supply water. What is the purpose of this additive?

options.text: To inactivate microbes.
To prevent tooth decay.
To reduce the corrosive effect of chlorine ions.
To prevent fouling of the water supply in the pipes.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, some toothpastes and dentifrices also contain the compound.

questions.stem: Iodophors used in personal health products and as a disinfectant are made______________.

options.text: of 2% solution of iodine and sodium iodide in ethanol
by dissolving molecular iodine in a dilute solution of phosphoric acid
by attaching iodine molecules to carriers such as polyvinylpyrrolidone

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. Option A- describes tincture iodine, which was used previously as a disinfectant, but it is an irritant.

sections.heading: Chemical methods: metal salts and peroxigens

questions.stem: The active ingredient of Bordeaux mixture (used in controlling fungal infections of grapevines) is/are ____________; one can use ______________ to kill algae.

options.text: silver nitrate/ copper sulfate
copper sulfate and lime/ copper sulfate
ferrous sulfate and alum/ sulfates of aluminum and potassium (alum)

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Other options: silver nitrate- topical antibacterial agent, ferrous sulfate (green vitriol)- to flocculate microbes in water; alum- astringent, may be used to to flocculate microbes in water.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements on the commonly used peroxygens is INCORRECT?

options.text: Ozone gas- water purification.
0.2% peracetic acid- for HLD of solid surfaces.
10% benzyl peroxide solution- astringent antiseptic.
Hydrogen peroxide vapor- sanitizing cooking utensils.
Sodium perborate in laundry detergents- HLD of clothes.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): E. Professor's explanation: Ans is E, the main purpose is bleaching, not necessarily disinfection. 3.5% hydrogen peroxide can also be used as an antiseptic. All these agents can be used as bleach under certain conditions.

questions.stem: Some detergents are non-biodegradable, yet people prefer detergents to soaps because _________; and of the detergents ________ may effectively kill many microbes include bacteria.

options.text: soap increases the surface tension of water/ CHAPS (a zwitterionic detergent)
soaps are more expensive than detergents/Nonidet P-40 (a nonionic detergent)
detergents work in hard water, soaps do not/ benzalkonium chloride (a quat).

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. Other options: Both soaps and detergents reduce the surface tension of water. CHAPS and Nonidet P-40 are used for protein extraction from cells. Soaps can be more expensive than some but not all detergents. Sodium dodecyl sulfate may not kill bacteria.

questions.stem: Which of the following are the most effective measures for preventing viral infections?

options.text: Vaccines approved by NIAID.
Handwashing and practicing proper personal hygiene.
Avoiding casual sex and intravenous recreational drug use.
wearing appropriate garb and using protective laboratory gears.
Food inspection, proper management of pets, pest control, and proper waste disposal.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A, if available. B-D are good and essential practices but none of them are 100% efficient in preventing viral infections.

questions.stem: The spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 is the ligand that binds to ACE2 receptors on the host cell. Which of the following may, in theory, increase the rate of attachment of SARS-CoV-2 to the host cells?

options.text: An antibody that binds the spike proteins of the virus.
A drug that activates the expression of the ACE2 gene.
An antibody that binds the ACE2 proteins of the host cells.
A synthetic peptide that mimics the ACE2 protein and binds the spike protein.
A synthetic peptide that mimics the spike protein and binds the ACE2 protein.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Excess ACE-2 on the cell surface would allow more viruses to bind the host cell.

sections.heading: Common antiviral drugs, their target, and mechanisms

questions.stem: Chloroquine binds to a potassium channel of the plasma membrane and interferes with membrane trafficking. Chloroquine most likely interferes with __________ of the virus replication cycle.

options.text: biosynthesis
penetration
attachment
uncoating
assembly

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, since the drug binds the plasma membrane, it most likely interferes with membrane phenomena such as the penetration of viruses into the host cell.

questions.stem: Amantadine binds the M proteins on the envelope of the influenza virus. Amantadine inhibits __________ of the replication cycle of influenza viruses.

options.text: biosynthesis
penetration
attachment
uncoating
assembly

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. The capsid of the virus must come out of the envelope of the virus. Amantadine binds the M protein and prevents uncoating.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a good attribute of nucleotide analogs as antiviral drugs?

options.text: Nucleotide analogs make the newly synthesized DNA or RNA highly fragile.
Nucleotide analogs increase the rate of mutation in the virus genomes.
Nucleotide analogs interfere with DNA or RNA replication.
Nucleotide analogs rapidly kill susceptible host cells.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. Killing all the host cells that can be infected could be gravely deleterious to the host organism.

questions.stem: Highly active antiretroviral therapy (HART) combines two or more antiviral drugs, and the therapy is highly effective. Which of the following is NOT a good reason for adopting combination antiviral therapy?

options.text: Multiple drugs in the mixture inhibit multiple drug targets of the virus.
The drug mixture prevents rapid mutation and evolution of the virus.
The drug cocktail prevents the development of viral drug resistance.
The toxicity of the combined drugs acts synergistically.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. If synergistic in toxicity, the combined toxicity will be higher then sum of toxicity of individual drugs.

questions.stem: Which of the following steps of the influenza virus replication cycle is inhibited by zanamivir?

options.text: Assembly of the nucleocapsid of the virus.
Budding of the virus particles out of the plasma membrane.
Separation of the egressed viruses from the plasma membrane of the progenitor cells.
Assembly of viral envelope glycoproteins and matrix proteins on the plasma membrane of the host cell.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. The hemagglutinin ligand of the virus binds the sialic acid of the host cell. The drug binds neuraminidase on the virus membrane and prevents the enzyme from cutting sialic acid of the host cell. As a result, the egressed virus remains attached to the progenitor host cell.

questions.stem: Which of the following cells has the most optimal conditions to establish an antiviral state?

options.text: A cell that has secreted interferons.
A cell that has been infected by a virus.
A cell has expressed receptors for interferons.
A cell that has its interferon receptors bound to secreted interferons.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. Interferon binding to the interferon receptor sends a signal that induces expression of proteins for the antiviral state.

questions.stem: A cell that has established an antiviral state. Which of these is not an expected activity of the cell?

options.text: Preventing transcription of viral genes or translation of viral proteins.
Replicating chromosomes and dividing by mitosis.
Destroying/modifying viral RNA and proteins.
Preventing entry or egress of the virus.
Preventing virus assembly.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Antiviral state also arrest cell cycle. The cell do not diuvide.

questions.stem: The following statements describe how interfering dsRNA inhibits the translation of viral mRNAs. One of the statements is INCORRECT. Which of the statements is that?

options.text: Dicer cuts the interfering dsRNA into small pieces about 25 bp.
RISC takes the 25 bp RNA fragments to use them as guide RNAs.
RISC hybridizes a guide RNA with the target mRNA of the virus.
Dicer cuts the viral mRNA that is hybridized with the guide RNA.
Ribosomes fail to translate the fragmented viral mRNA (the mRNA disintegrates).

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. RISC cuts the mRNA hybridized to the guide RNA.

questions.stem: RNA interference (RNAi) drugs have been approved for treating certain diseases. Which of the following is the most pressing problem of RNAi therapy?

options.text: Problem with the stability of dsRNA molecules.
Synthesis and packing of dsRNA and efficacy of the drug.
Healthy cells receiving the dsRNA (i.e., synthesis of excess interferons).
Delivery of dsRNA inside the target cells in the specific tissues of specific organs.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D. dsRNAs are relatively stable; synthesis of dsRNA is easy, and the drugs are highly effective in the test tube. Interferon storm can be managed for a short term, but inserting dsRNA specifically in the target cells avoiding all other healthy cells of the body is the problem to be solved.

questions.stem: Passive immunization (i.e., injecting specific antibodies) targets mainly the _______ step of the virus replication cycle.

options.text: biosynthesis
penetration
attachment
assembly
egress

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C, because the antibodies injected into the patient body bind ligands on the surface of the viruses and prevent the viruses from binding the receptor of the host cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following antibodies has no use in preventing or treating SARS CoV-2 infections?

options.text: Anti-SARS CoV-2 IgG antibodies separated from all other proteins in the plasma of a donor.
Serum of volunteers who have never been infected by the virus.
Serum of a healthy horse experimentally infected by the virus.
Whole serum of a person previously infected by the virus.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. This sample has antibodies to other pathogens but no antibodies to the SARS CoV-2. To be effective, an antibody must bind the virus ligands and neutralize the virus. Human, horse, or mouse antibodies can be used for the purpose as long as the antibodies specifically bind antigens of SARS CoV-2.

questions.stem: An antimicrobial chemotherapeutic agent should be a magic bullet. What does a magic bullet do?

options.text: It would kill/inactivate microbes effectively.
It would be harmless to the host organism.
It would be harmless to the resident biota.
It would have all these attributes

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D, by definition.

questions.stem: The first antimicrobial chemotherapeutic agent with the properties of a magic bullet that was applied to treat bacterial infections in humans was__________ and it was developed by ___________.

options.text: salvarsan/ Paul Ehrlich (1854-1915)
prontosil/ Gerhard Domagk (1895-1964)
penicillin/ Alexander Fleming (1885-1955)
streptomycin/ Selman Waxman (1888-1973)

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, Gerhard Domagk used it in 1930s. Paul Ehrlich used salvarsan in the 1910s but the drug was highly toxic to humans, penicillin was isolated and tested in the 1940s, streptomycin was also isolated and tested in the 1940s.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most suitable target for developing antibacterial chemotherapeutic agents?

options.text: Lipid synthesis and membrane dynamics.
Cell wall synthesis and maintenance.
DNA replication and recombination.
RNA transcription and processing.
Protein synthesis and processing.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, because human cells lack a cell wall. Bacteria and human cells share all the other attributes.

questions.stem: Why bacterial DNA replication is not an ideal target for developing antibacterial drugs.

options.text: No known agent inhibits bacterial DNA polymerase.
DNA replication in bacteria and human cells has many similarities.
Agents that may inhibit bacterial DNA replication are potential mutagens.
Agents that inhibit bacterial DNA replication cannot penetrate the bacterial cell wall.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, by eliminating the other three options. Many agents can enter bacterial cells and inhibit DNA polymerase; not all of them can be mutagens, but most of the agents may inhibit the DNA polymerase of human cells.

questions.stem: Why are membrane-active antibiotics such as polymyxins, daptomycin, and gramicidin usually used in treating surface wounds and not as orally and parenterally (injected) administered drugs? Note: Only the best answer will be scored.

options.text: The drugs are not absorbed if taken orally or injected.
The drugs may damage the host cell’s membranes.
The drugs are made of a polypeptide and a lipid.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. The drugs create holes in the plasma membrane or alter membrane polarity and thus can be very toxic. The drugs are made mainly of polypeptides, so they should soluble, and given orally or parenterally. Daptomycin and polymyxin are occasionally used in treating multidrug-resistant bacterial infections.

questions.stem: Isoniazid and ethionamide inhibit mycolic acid synthesis; thus, they are effective against _______________.

options.text: all actinobacteria
acid-fast bacteria
broad range of bacteria
bacteria lacking a cell wall Antibacterials: Beta-lactams

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, because they (including Mycobacterium tuberculosis) have mycolic acid attached to the arabinogalactan cell wall. Many but not all actinobacteria have mycolic acid, G(-) bacteria and most G(+) bacteria other than actinobacteria lack mycolic acid (see Chapter 3).

questions.stem: Which reactions or processes of bacterial cell wall synthesis do beta-lactam antibiotics inhibit?

options.text: Synthesis of polyalanine oligopeptides.
Synthesis of the NAG-NAM disaccharide.
Attachment of NAG-NAM disaccharide to an existing polysaccharide.
Cross-linking of two amino acids of the oligopeptides of two NAM entities.
Transport of NAG-NAM disaccharide units outside of the plasma membrane.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): D. Professor's explanation: Ans is D, as observed. It is also known that bacitracin inhibits option D, vancomycin inhibits option C.

questions.stem: Why do many physicians prefer amoxicillin-clavulanate to amoxicillin in treating bacterial infections?

options.text: Clavulanate inhibits beta-lactamases.
Clavulanate inhibits bacterial transpeptidase.
Clavulanate reduces the toxicity of amoxicillin.
Clavulanate increases the bioavailability of amoxicillin.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A. Clavulanate, sulbactam, and tazobactam are often added to beta-lactam antibiotics because these agents inhibit bacterial beta-lactamases.

questions.stem: A strain of Staphylococcus aureus became resistant to methicillin because it produces a beta-lactamase enzyme. How does the beta-lactamase enzyme make the bacterium methicillin-resistant?

options.text: The enzyme cuts open the thiazolidine ring of methicillin.
The enzyme cuts C-N bond and opens the beta-lactam ring of methicillin.
The enzyme binds methicillin and prevents transpeptidases from binding the antibiotics.
The enzyme chemically modifies methicillin by attaching a methyl group to the beta-lactamase ring.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. None of the beta-lactam antibiotics works if the beta-lactam ring is opened (a beta-lactam antibiotic with a damaged beta-lactam ring fails to bind transpeptidase enzymes of the bacterium).

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a purpose of designing semi-synthetic or fully synthetic antibiotics?

options.text: Reduce drug toxicity.
Reduce drug bioavailability.
Making the drugs broad-spectrum.
Making the drugs resistant to bacterial enzymes.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, the purpose is to increase bioavailability (the proportion of a taken dose of the drug that enters the blood).

questions.stem: Which of the following antibiotics can be used in treating Mycoplasma pneumoniae?

options.text: Cephalosporins or cephamycins (3rd, 4th or 5th generation).
Aminopenicillins such as carbenicillin.
Monobactams such as meropenem.
Fully synthetic carbapenems.
None of these antibiotics.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): E. Professor's explanation: Ans is E, because Mycoplasma pneumoniae lacks a cell wall.

sections.heading: Other inhibitors of cell wall synthesis

questions.stem: Which of these statements about vancomycin is INCORRECT?

options.text: It is made of amino acids and sugars.
It is only effective against G(+) bacteria.
It is effective against MERSA and VERSA.
It prevents the crosslinking of oligopeptides of the bacterial cell wall.
It is effective against the naturally drug-resistant soil bacterium Clostridium difficile.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C, it is effective against MERSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), and but it is obviously not effective against vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (VERSA).

questions.stem: Ethambutol inhibits arabinogalactan synthesis. Which of the bacteria should the drug be effective against?

options.text: G(+) bacteria such as actinobacteria.
G(-) bacteria such as proteobacteria.
G(-) bacteria such as mycoplasmas.
Spirochetes.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A, because actinobacteria have arabinogalactan (in addition to peptidoglycan) in the cell wall.

questions.stem: Cycloserine is related to a/an________, and it is used as a second line of antibiotics to treat__________ if other antibiotics do not work.

options.text: fatty acid/ anaerobic bacterial infections of soft tissues
amino acid/multidrug-resistant mycobacteria
nucleotide/ disseminated bacterial infections
monosaccharide/ mixed bacterial infections Inhibitors of DNA replication

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B, is a chemically modified serine (one of the 20 common amino acids), the drug is extremely toxic, so it is used in treating multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis if other antibiotics do not work.

questions.stem: How do fluoroquinolones inhibit DNA replication in bacteria?

options.text: They inhibit bacterial helicase.
They inhibit bacterial DNA polymerase.
They inhibit bacterial DNA topoisomerase.
They inhibit the bacterial DNA sliding clamp.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C, also known as topoisomerase IV.

questions.stem: Metronidazole binds to DNA and causes single-stranded DNA breaks. Why is this a medical concern, and why is the drug effective only against anaerobic bacteria and protozoa?

options.text: The drug may create drug-resistant bacteria; aerobes do not absorb the drug.
A high dose of the drug is necessary to make the drug effective; oxygen destroys the drug.
The drug may mutate the host cell’s chromosomes; only anaerobes have nitroreductase to activate the drug.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C, in the mice model, the drug produces tumors. The drug is bactericidal (so it does not create many mutant bacteria), oxygen does not destroy the drug and any cell can absorb the drug.

questions.stem: Clofazimine, one of the most effective drugs to treat leprosy, binds guanine residues. Which of these bacterial activities does the drug directly affect?

options.text: Lipid synthesis
DNA replication.
RNA transcription.
Protein synthesis and processing.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Since it binds guanine residues of DNA, it most likely affects DNA replication.

questions.stem: Mutations in which of these genes would make a bacterium resistant to rifamycin, and why is rifamycin always used in combination therapy?

options.text: The DNA polymerase gene; the drug is highly toxic.
The DNA helicase gene, the drug is unstable if used alone.
The RNA polymerase gene; bacteria readily become resistant to the drug.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. The drug inhibits RNA polymerase. A mutant RNA polymerase can be resistant to the drug. The drug is stable. It is toxic but that is not why combined therapy is used.

questions.stem: Aminoglycosides bind the 23S rRNA of the 30S ribosome particles. Which of the following steps of protein synthesis do aminoglycosides most likely inhibit?

options.text: Translation initiation.
Translation elongation.
Translation termination.
Post-termination event (such as ribosome recycling).

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): A. Professor's explanation: Ans is A, because the drugs bind 30S ribosome particles and 30S ribosome particles are needed for translation initiation. Even if protein synthesis initiates with drug-bound 30S ribosomes, translation elongation becomes error- prone and suffers from premature termination.

questions.stem: (a) Which of the following aminoglycosides is nontoxic, and (b) which of the aminoglycosides is used in treating/preventing Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections of the lung of cystic fibrosis patients?

options.text: (a) Kanamycin/(b) Neomycin.
(a) Neomycin/ (b) Streptomycin.
(a) Streptomycin/ (b) gentamycin.
(a) Streptomycin/ (b) Plazomicin.
(a) None of the aminoglycosides/ (b) Tobramycin.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): E. Professor's explanation: Ans is E. questions.stem: Which of the following is the most rapid method of spreading bacterial antibiotic resistance among different strains and species of pathogenic and nonpathogenic bacteria?

options.text: Gene mutations and vertical gene transfer.
Lateral gene transfer via bacterial conjugation.
Lateral gene transfer via bacterial transduction.
Lateral gene transfer via bacterial transformation.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): B. Professor's explanation: Ans is B. Many antibiotic resistance genes are present in R factor plasmids. Although bacterial conjugation is conducted by F factor plasmids, many F factor plasmids are also R factor plasmids, and the F factors plasmid helps some R factors plasmids to move during conjugation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most likely the primary reason for bacterial antibiotic resistance in the developed countries of East Asia, Western Europe, Australia, and North America?

Use of antibiotics in animal feed and fermentation industries.
Use of improper doses of antibiotics and use of expired/outdated antibiotics.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. questions.stem: According to the WHO, bacterial antibiotic resistance is currently at a crisis point, or human civilization is already in the post-antibiotic era. Which of the following is the most critical step nations would take to overcome this crisis?

options.text: Minimize antibiotic use.
Inactivate antibiotics before disposal.
Develop new and more effective antibiotics.
Stop agricultural and industrial use of antibiotics.
Rigorously enforce the drug laws and increase public education on antibiotic use.

questions.answerRationale: Official key (MCI for OLQs 5-8 Answered & Explained.pdf): C. Professor's explanation: Ans is C. The other measure may not remove already antibiotic-resistant strains of bacteria. Thus, new antibiotics and other measures are needed to overcome the current antibiotic crisis.
questions.priorRationale: Course text (Table 8.14, 'Developing new antibiotics'): 'All the above measures may not eliminate bacterial strains that are already antibiotic-resistant ... some resistant strains retain the resistance even after growing in antibiotic-free conditions. Thus, at least some new and highly effective antibiotics are needed to eliminate those strains. ONCE THOSE STRAINS ARE UNDER CONTROL, rational use of antibiotics and public education may prevent another antibiotic crisis.' The stem says the crisis has ALREADY arrived ('currently at a crisis point, or ... already in the post-antibiotic era') and asks what is most critical to OVERCOME it, so new antibiotics (C); enforcement and public education only help prevent a repeat.
